attempts.summary: Used Ansible (run from node2, the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed, acting as control node) to blacklist the usb-storage kernel module on node1. The playbook creates /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with `blacklist usb-storage` and `install usb-storage /bin/false`, runs update-initramfs -u, and ensures the module isn't currently loaded via community.general.modprobe. Had to first bootstrap sshd on node1 (missing host keys) and set up key-based root SSH from node2, since the default ansible.cfg assumed a pre-provisioned 'antrieb' user that doesn't exist on this vanilla Ubuntu image. Verified modprobe usb-storage fails (rc=1) and the module stays unloaded, both before and after restarting node1. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured boot_id baselines, restarted each node one at a time, confirmed boot_id changed after each restart, and verified recovery (blacklist enforced on node1; ansible control tooling and connectivity to node1 recovered on node2, confirmed via an idempotent playbook re-run showing changed=0).
